The test image shows a corn ear with damage at the **tip**: brownish/rotted kernels at the tip with whitish-gray mold, while the rest of the ear has normal yellow kernels. This is a **seed/pod** affected part.

Key features:
- Damage concentrated at the ear tip
- Brownish, discolored, shrunken kernels at tip
- Whitish-grayish material/mold around damaged area
- No bright pink/red, no obvious olive-green powder

Top candidates: Fusarium_Disease (whitish-pink at tip), Aspergillus_Ear_Rot (olive-green at tip), Gibberella_Disease (red/pink at tip).

The whitish mold without strong pink or green color points most toward Fusarium. Let me view one reference.

The Fusarium reference shows whitish mold scattered mid-ear with starburst patterns. The test image differs — damage is at the tip with brownish rotted kernels and some white/gray material, which is still consistent with Fusarium ear rot (tip location, whitish growth). The lack of bright pink rules out Gibberella, and no olive-green powder rules out Aspergillus.
